newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK housing block fire kills seven, injures 38.
newsitem.headline: HK housing block fire kills seven, injures 38.

text.p: Residents of a Hong Kong high-rise apartment building squatted on window ledges and clung to drainpipes on Tuesday to escape a fire that killed at least seven people, including two babies.
The fire broke out at lunchtime on the sixth floor of the 20-storey block in Kowloon district and spread to the floor below. Firefighters took four hours to put out the blaze.
The dead included two baby girls, four women, one aged 65, and one man.
"They died from inhaling a lot of thick smoke. They did not die from burns. Their burns were quite minor," said a doctor at one of two hospitals taking the casualties.
The district police chief said most of the building's fire doors had been left open.
A government spokesman said at least 38 people also were injured, including a fireman, and had been taken to hospital.
"Latest information revealed that seven persons were killed and 38 others were injured in the fire," a government spokesman said, adding that two were in intensive care.
A hospital spokesman said the firefighter was in satisfactory condition.

At the height of the blaze, terrified residents threatened by smoke on the upper floors clung to external pipes and scrambled on to ledges and flimsy racks used to dry clothes, shouting out to firemen in scenes relayed live by television.
Firemen ferried swooning housewives and howling children and even a dog down an extension ladder to safety.
The cause of the fire was not immediately known.
But district police chief Bonnie Smith told reporters one theory was the fire might have been started by a cigarette and that it had spread quickly because fire doors were not shut.
"Most of the smoke doors were left open, and this is believed to be what caused so many casualties," she said.
Hong Kong has suffered some of its worst building fires in recent months, including two major disasters.
In November, a fire in a building in Kowloon's Nathan Road "golden mile" tourist shopping street killed 39 people and injured 81.
A fire in a karaoke bar in January killed 17 people in Kowloon's Tsimshatsui entertainment district.
British Governor Chris Patten hurried to the hospital to console the injured and said more be done to improve safety standards and awareness.
"The best tribute we could pay to those who have been bereaved is to try our hardest to stop this sort of thing happening with such appalling regularity in Hong Kong," he said.
"The government has to do more to raise safety standards for the community."
